findings.title: totalPages off-by-one creates a phantom empty last page
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. The correct formula is Math.ceil(user_count / limit). Consequence: showingLast is never true on the real last page, so the 'next' arrow stays enabled; clicking it sets offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count) = user_count (see the next action at line 33), the server returns an empty member list, and the admin is shown an empty page '3/3' with no members. The same clamp in the next action should cap at the last valid offset, not at user_count.

findings.title: members action does not validate limit/offset; negative values cause 500s
findings.body: The members action now always applies user-supplied limit and offset to the query (limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i; offset = params[:offset].to_i) with no clamping. A request like GET /groups/<name>/members.json?offset=-1 or ?limit=-1 passes a negative value to ActiveRecord's limit/offset, which produces invalid SQL and a 500 error on a public, unauthenticated-for-visible-groups endpoint. There is also no upper bound on limit, so limit=1000000 dumps an arbitrarily large member list in one query. Values should be clamped (e.g. offset = [offset, 0].max, limit capped at a sane maximum). There are also no controller specs covering this new pagination endpoint (pagination correctness, negative input).

findings.title: create silently drops the alias_level submitted by the client
findings.body: The admin UI's group form always shows the alias-level combo box, and the client model's asJSON() sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups, but the create action only reads params[:name] and params[:visible]. An admin who sets an alias level on the 'New Group' form and saves will silently get a group with the default alias_level of 0; the value is discarded without any error. The update action accepts alias_level, so the asymmetry is clearly an oversight. Either accept and apply params[:alias_level] in create or stop sending/collecting it for unsaved groups.

findings.title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove and deletes the join record directly
findings.body: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which deletes the has_many :through join records at the SQL level, bypassing any logic in Group#remove (the method the previous controller code called, and still the counterpart of the group.add(user) call used by add_members in this same controller). If Group#remove performs bookkeeping such as clearing primary_group/title references or invalidating caches, that work is silently skipped and user records can be left referencing a group they are no longer in. The add and remove paths should go through the same model API (group.add / group.remove) to keep side effects symmetric.

findings.title: PUT/POST /admin/groups silently ignore the former group[usernames] membership parameter
findings.body: Previously PUT /admin/groups/:id and POST /admin/groups accepted group[usernames] and applied membership changes; the new controller drops that parameter entirely and moves membership to the new PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members endpoints. The old PATCH-based incremental update (changes[:add]/changes[:delete]) is also removed along with its tests. Any existing API consumer (scripts, plugins) that sends group[usernames] will now receive a 200 success while the membership change is silently ignored — a no-op data change reported as success. Since this is an intentional redesign, at minimum the removal should be called out, and ignoring the parameter with a success response is the worst option; an explicit 4xx for unrecognized membership parameters would be safer.

findings.title: After removing a member on the last page, the member list goes blank instead of stepping back a page
findings.body: removeMember calls findMembers() with the current offset unchanged. If the admin was on the last page and that page's last member is removed, user_count drops below offset (e.g. count 51 -> 50 with offset 50), so the reloaded list is empty while the stale offset is retained (the server echoes the requested offset back in meta). The UI then shows an empty '2/2' page and the admin must click 'previous' manually. After a successful removal, offset should be recomputed against the new total (e.g. offset = Math.min(offset, Math.max(total - limit, 0))).

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember have no failure handlers, so server errors fail silently
findings.body: Both addMembers and removeMember only attach a .then() success handler to the AJAX call. If the server rejects the request (422 for automatic groups, validation failure, network error), the promise rejects with no handler: the user gets no feedback even though they confirmed the action in a bootbox dialog, and the member list is not reloaded or corrected. A rejection handler showing the returned errors (and keeping state consistent) is needed.

findings.title: remove_member spec issues PUT while the route is DELETE
findings.body: The spec exercises remove_member with 'xhr :put, :remove_member, ...', but the route wired up in config/routes.rb is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member". Controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes while exercising a verb that cannot reach the action in production. It should be xhr :delete so the spec reflects the real contract.
